method: Full-text adjudication of the 100 defenses that untested_defense_classification.json put in 'names_registry_attack' (no confirmed pair, but the paper names a registry attack). Three readers, one label each with a verbatim quote: ran_named_attack / evaluated_other / no_evaluation / unsure. Precision-first: a pair needs the paper's own experiment to run the defense against the named attack.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: Sec. 7 Evaluation: 'Five scenarios embed indirect prompt injections in public forum content' ... APPA 'dropping Attack Success Rate (ASR) from 31%-' ; also 'We instrumented AgentDojo (all four suites, tool_knowledge attack)'
confirmed_pairs.note: Own bench-corp benchmark with embedded IPI scenarios, ASR reported per arm across four models; AgentDojo tool_knowledge also run.

confirmed_pairs.defense: Agent Privilege Separation (Reader/Actor two-agent isolation + JSON formatting)
confirmed_pairs.evidence: Sec. 4 Results / abstract: 'We replicate Microsoft's LLMail-Inject ... full pipeline achieves 0% ASR on the evaluated benchmark (attack success rate); two-agent isolation alone achieves 0.31% ASR'
confirmed_pairs.note: Evaluated on LLMail-Inject, an indirect prompt injection benchmark where the injection lives in an email body.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: Sec. 4 Experiments: 'we modify the retrieved contexts in the NQ dataset to contain factually [conflicting] ... incorporate ConFiQA (Bi et al., 2024a) and MQuAKE ... These tasks introduce counterfactual information that conflicts with the model's parametric knowledge.'
confirmed_pairs.note: Quantitative knowledge-conflict evaluation (NQ counterfactual, ConFiQA, MQuAKE; ConR/MR metrics).

confirmed_pairs.evidence: Sec. V.C Causal Tracing Analysis: '68% of hallucinations originate from information in the 40-60% context region ... CoM reduces middle-context hallucinations by 81%.'
confirmed_pairs.note: Six long-context benchmarks (LongBench-QA, InfiniteBench, ...) with a position-resolved middle-context hallucination measurement; thin short paper, numbers not tied to a controlled position sweep.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: Sec. 6.1 Experimental setup: 'Knowledge Poisoning. Our knowledge poisoning setup is adapted from PoisonedRAG [62].' (attack table lists Knowledge Poisoning / PoisonedRAG [62])
confirmed_pairs.note: Detection AUROC/MAcc reported for knowledge-poisoning queries built from PoisonedRAG on MS MARCO/HotpotQA etc. Adapted (not verbatim) PoisonedRAG.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: Sec. 4 (quadrants) / Experiment: 'Known-Noisy (KN, q in Kparam \ Kretr): The model possesses the correct answer, but retrieval fails or provides noisy context ... Ideally, the model should prioritize internal knowledge'; Wiki Event: 'we also synthesize counterfactual contexts by systematically perturbing key entities in the gold contexts to simulate realistic scenarios of noisy or conflicting retrieval.'
confirmed_pairs.note: Borderline: conflict is measured via a stratified Known-Noisy quadrant on NQ/TriviaQA/WebQ (natural retrieval) and perturbed counterfactual contexts, not a standard conflict benchmark.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: Experiment Settings: 'MuSiQue and SQuAD ... are from KRE (Ying et al., 2024) which introduce fact-level knowledge conflicts ... FaithEval (Ming et al., 2025) introduces logical-level conflicts'
confirmed_pairs.note: Main evaluation is on counterfactual knowledge-conflict benchmarks (KRE MuSiQue/SQuAD, FaithEval, RealtimeQA).

confirmed_pairs.evidence: Sec. 5 Security metrics: 'we inject the test sets with these prompts. Each test sample and prompt injection pair yields three test cases: one with the prompt injection added to the start of the input, one at the end of the input, and one at a random position in the middle'
confirmed_pairs.note: Injections (HackAPrompt + hand-crafted) are placed in the task's untrusted data input (reviews, code, etc.), i.e., indirect-style injection; ASR drops from 87% to <0.5%.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: Experiments, Datasets and Metrics: 'We adopt NaturalQuestions-Open following LITM setting ... [golden document] placed at 0%, 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% positions in the prompt to simulate the positional variation.'
confirmed_pairs.note: Runs the Lost-in-the-Middle protocol directly (NQ-Open, gold-position sweep) plus LongBench; contextual misguidance is the paper's own named failure.

confirmed_pairs.defense: ProbeRAG (knowledge pruning + latent conflict probing + conflict-aware attention)
confirmed_pairs.evidence: Datasets: 'We evaluate ProbeRAG on three datasets. ConFiQA (Bi et al., 2025a) is a benchmark designed to assess contextual faithfulness in ... tasks in which the context includes one and multiple counterfactuals. FaithEval ...'
confirmed_pairs.note: Main evaluation on counterfactual knowledge-conflict benchmarks (ConFiQA MC/MR/QA, FaithEval) plus SQuAD.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: Datasets: 'We further evaluate our model on ConfiQA (Bi et al., 2024) to examine its generalization capabilities, including three subsets: Question Answering (QA), Multi-hop Reasoning (MR), and MultiConflicts (MC).'
confirmed_pairs.note: Knowledge-conflict pair holds (ConFiQA MC/MR/QA plus a counterfactual case study); the other named attack, self-induced context poisoning, is not run.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: Datasets: 'We use two widely adopted open-domain question-answering datasets with knowledge conflicts NQSwap (Longpre et al., 2021) and Macnoise (Hong et al., 2024)'
confirmed_pairs.note: Steering control measured on knowledge-conflict sets NQSwap and Macnoise.

confirmed_pairs.defense: UNNAMED: Digital forensic analysis framework for post-hoc IPI attack identification from agent execution logs
confirmed_pairs.evidence: Experimental testbed: 'we use gpt-4o-2024-05-13 and important_instructions_no_names non-adaptive IPI attack to execute the benign and injection tasks'; 'preliminary results are shown in Table I' (precision/recall/F1 per suite)
confirmed_pairs.note: Post-hoc forensic detector scored on AgentDojo logs generated with the important_instructions IPI attack; preliminary, but quantitative.

confirmed_pairs.defense: Agent Sentry (structural classifier + allowlist + LLM judge)
confirmed_pairs.evidence: 6.8 Delivery Mechanism Invariance, Table 8: "ImportantInstructions 532 [attacks] 91.5 [ABR]; DirectAttack 78 92.3; InjecAgentAttack 65 90.8"
confirmed_pairs.note: Evaluated on AgentDojo/AgentDyn and its Agent-Sentry Bench with indirect prompt injection (important-instructions, InjecAgent attacks); attack block rate reported. Missed pair.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: Appendix B, Table 17 (Recall by attack type): "indirect 2,676 ... 67.34% ... 97.12%"; "two labels, direct and indirect, account for 3,393 of the 3,479 malicious records"
confirmed_pairs.note: Detector evaluated on a 5,000-sample corpus whose largest malicious class is labelled indirect injection (embedded in MCP tool-response framings); per-type recall reported. Missed pair, though corpus labels are inherited and loosely defined.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: 4.3 Effectiveness under Knowledge Conflicts: "To further investigate the effectiveness of Conflict-Aware RAG in knowledge conflict scenarios, we compare Vanilla RAG ... Figure 3: Performance comparison on SQuAD under knowledge conflict scenarios"
confirmed_pairs.note: Reports per-category results (Supplemented by Document / Interfered by Document) where retrieved context and parametric answer disagree; natural conflicts partitioned, not a constructed counterfactual set. Missed pair.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: Appendix C: "Agent Goal Hijack The attacker hosts a spoofed website embedding a malicious prompt. When the agent ingests the page during task execution, the prompt hijacks the agent's goal"; Table 4 rows S1/S2/S4 (1+2+8) report path- and node-level TP/FP/FN for MAScope
confirmed_pairs.note: Detection evaluated on 10 self-built LangGraph scenarios (14,927 log records); several attack cases are indirect prompt injection via web pages/resumes (Fig. 8). Missed pair; own-built attacks, small n. Self-induced context poisoning not tested.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: 5.1 Threat Emulator: "we also consider a proactive attack scenario where an attacker injects a prompt in their response to request sensitive data. Here, four prompt injection strategies from the AgentDojo benchmark are used ... 'Ignore previous instructions,' InjecAgent-style overrides, 'TODO' instructions, and important diversion messages"; Table 1 Proactive PVR 75%->0% (HospitalGPT), 100%->0% (TravelAgent)
confirmed_pairs.note: Injections arrive in responses from a compromised peer agent (or tool), using AgentDojo/InjecAgent payloads; policy-violation rate reported. Counts as IPI if peer-agent messages are treated as untrusted context; small n (20 tasks).

confirmed_pairs.evidence: 4.1 Real-Document Benchmark: "We construct a benchmark of 122 tasks spanning five professional domains. Each task pairs a real retrieved document with a domain-camouflaged payload targeting a distinct malicious goal"; Abstract: PARSE "achieves 15.6% attack success rate"
confirmed_pairs.note: ASR of injections embedded in retrieved documents (domain-camouflaged IPI variant) across eight defense conditions. Missed pair.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: 5.1 Experiment Setup: "Adversarial Prompts (AP) pair a legitimate surface task with an indirect prompt injection embedded in a realistic carrier such as a document, web page, tool output, email, or CRM record"; Security-relevant recovery: "The gain is largest on AP, where coverage rises from 0.520 to 0.652"
confirmed_pairs.note: Interpretability monitor: measured how well it recovers injected instructions from activations on 250 self-built IPI examples. It measures detection/recovery, not attack prevention. Missed pair if a monitor counts as a defense.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: 4 Experimental Results, Depth-Robust Needle Retrieval: "Figure 4 demonstrates QwenLong-CPRS-enhanced Qwen2.5-7b-Instruct's performance in the Needle-in-a-Haystack paradigm across full-spectrum depth variations (0% to 100%) and context lengths (32K to 1M tokens)"
confirmed_pairs.note: Abstract frames the method against 'lost in the middle'; the NIAH depth sweep varies evidence position, which is the positional test. Single-needle NIAH rather than Liu et al.'s multi-document QA; counts if a depth sweep is accepted as the lost-in-the-middle test.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: 6.7 Knowledge Selection Performance: "Further analysis is conducted on the issue of knowledge conflict before and after RPO ... In Cluster B and C, which involve knowledge conflicts, SFT does not achieve a positive advancement, while RPO has shown a significant improvement in knowledge selection"
confirmed_pairs.note: Main results are end-task QA on PopQA etc.; Sec. 6.7/Fig. 3 partitions instances where parametric and retrieved answers conflict and reports knowledge-selection accuracy. Natural conflicts, not a constructed counterfactual set. Missed pair.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: 2 A Knowledge-Conflict Benchmark: "We construct the query-context pool from five conflict-QA datasets, including ConFiQA with three sub-tasks (QA, MR, MC), ConflictQA-PopQA [30] (abbr. ConflictQA), ConflictBank, and the TriviaQA and Natural Questions (NQ) subsets"; 4 Experiments reports Acc/CF/KF/MFS
confirmed_pairs.note: PDF found by title (Trust or Abstain A Self-Aware RAG Approach.pdf). Core evaluation is PK-vs-CK conflict on ConFiQA/ConflictBank etc. Clear missed pair.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: Abstract: "Across seven benchmarks TCR improves conflict detection (+5-18 F1), raises knowledge-gap recovery by +21.4 pp and cuts misleading-context overrides by -29.3 pp"; Benchmarks: "... ConflictBank ... and a single-document NQ setting"
confirmed_pairs.note: Context-memory conflict is the evaluated condition (ConflictBank, built ConflictTQA, KILT). Clear missed pair.

confirmed_pairs.defense: UNNAMED: Embedding-based semantic context analysis detector for IPI
confirmed_pairs.evidence: Abstract: "We also provide a dataset of 70,000 samples, constructed using 35,000 malicious instances from the Benchmark for Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks (BIPIA) and 35,000 benign instances generated using ChatGPT-4o-mini"
confirmed_pairs.note: Detector classification results on BIPIA indirect injections (Section 4). Clear missed pair.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: 6.3 Results: 'CD2 leads to a 2.05% and 2.70% Recall improvement on NQ-Inco and TriviaQA-Inco ... For knowledge conflicts between internal memory and external sources, we create NQ-Inco and TriviaQA-Inco datasets'
confirmed_pairs.note: CD2 is evaluated directly on self-built context-vs-memory conflict sets (NQ/TriviaQA-Inco, -Conf); the named failure is the paper's own test condition.

confirmed_pairs.defense: CRVA-TGRAG (Conflict Resolution in Vulnerability Analysis via Teacher-Guided RAG)
confirmed_pairs.evidence: Sec. 5 Experiments: 'we integrated and designed evaluation metrics to effectively assess the system's ability to resolve knowledge conflicts'; contributions: 'The dataset includes 1,260 pairwise conflict CVE items that have been published and modified over the past decade.'
confirmed_pairs.note: Evaluated on its own CVE conflict dataset (stale parametric CVE knowledge vs updated retrieved records); accuracy/faithfulness gains reported. Domain-specific, but the named conflict is the test condition.

confirmed_pairs.defense: FATE (on-policy self-evolving repair framework) with Pareto-Front Policy Optimization (PFPO)
confirmed_pairs.evidence: Task settings: 'We evaluate on AgentDojo and AgentHarm [9, 3], covering indirect prompt injection and harmful agentic requests.' Abstract: 'reduces attack success rate by 33.5%'
confirmed_pairs.note: Clear missed pair: FATE is measured on AgentDojo injection tasks (ASR/TSR) against Tool Filter and PI Detector baselines.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: Datasets & Metrics: 'ConFiQA (Bi et al., 2024), a dataset designed for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) scenarios, incorporating knowledge conflicts through counterfactual passages ... evaluate it on ConFiQA'
confirmed_pairs.note: GenDiE is scored on ConFiQA counterfactual-context conflicts (Table 1).

confirmed_pairs.evidence: Sec. 4.2 (Structured Query benchmark): 'Following the approach of Chen et al. (2024), we evaluate indirect prompt injection attacks on models trained on the Alpaca dataset'; results: 'achieves an average robust accuracy improvement of up to 15.75% against indirect prompt injection'
confirmed_pairs.note: ISE is measured on in-domain and OOD indirect prompt injection (StruQ-style Naive/Ignore/Escape/Completion) on both benchmarks.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: Datasets: 'benchmark datasets drawn from two comprehensive collections: ConflictBank and KRE. ConflictBank (Su et al., 2024) provides three specialized ...'; Intro: 'Extensive experiments on five widely-used knowledge conflict benchmark datasets'
confirmed_pairs.note: Micro-Act is scored on ConflictBank (misinformation/temporal/semantic) and KRE context-vs-memory conflicts.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: 5.1.1 Benchmarks: 'We use the widely adopted OpenPromptInjection [6] and AgentDojo [37] benchmarks.'; Table 1: 'Results of PromptLocate and the baselines for seven attacks in the OpenPromptInjection benchmark' (row: Combined Attack)
confirmed_pairs.note: Clear missed pair for Combined Attack (main results + adaptive Combined Attack in 5.3). Relinking is not run (Relinking post-dates/cites PromptLocate as a baseline).

confirmed_pairs.defense: SecureClaw (dual-boundary: effect-sink authorization + read-boundary plaintext confinement)
confirmed_pairs.evidence: Sec. 5 / Table 2: 'Benchmark evaluation on same-harness baselines (gpt-4o-mini)' ... 'On effectful benchmarks it reaches 0% ASR on ASB and 0.64% ASR on AgentDojo (4/629).'
confirmed_pairs.note: Clear missed pair: SecureClaw measured on AgentDojo and ASB indirect-injection tasks vs IPIGuard, DRIFT, Faramesh.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: 4.1 Datasets: 'ConflictQA (Xie et al. 2023) (2,839 samples): Each q contains internal knowledge "parametric memory" and conflicting external context "counter memory"'
confirmed_pairs.note: Swin-VIB scored on ConflictQA, DRUID and TruthfulQA conflicting-context settings.

confirmed_pairs.evidence: Datasets: 'We conduct experiments on four datasets that encompass various knowledge-intensive tasks and conflict scenarios. FaithEval ... counterfactual contexts ... MuSiQue and SQuAD come from [KRE] ... fact-level knowledge conflicts ... RealtimeQA focuses on temporal conflicts'
confirmed_pairs.note: TruthfulRAG is scored on context-vs-memory conflict sets (FaithEval counterfactual, KRE MuSiQue/SQuAD, RealtimeQA).

confirmed_pairs.evidence: Threat model: 'This reflects indirect prompt injection ... LLMail-Inject captures and tests this threat model'; Abstract: 'we assemble and re-annotate the comprehensive LLMail-Inject dataset ... greater than 93% accuracy in classifying prompt injections'
confirmed_pairs.note: Detector scored on LLMail-Inject email-borne indirect injection payloads (offline classification of payload text, no agent loop).

weak_pairs_not_counted.defense: PACEvolve - Hierarchical Context Management (HCM) component specifically
weak_pairs_not_counted.evidence: Sec. 4.3 Ablation studies: 'The vanilla implementation appends a summary of the proposed solution and experiment results of each iteration ... We then gradually add hierarchical context management ... Adding hierarchical context erasure significantly improves the mean and best-performing evolutionary processes.'
weak_pairs_not_counted.note: Self-pair: the attack is PACEvolve's own coined failure mode; HCM is ablated against the polluting vanilla history (10 runs, Symbolic Regression). Effect measured by task score, not a direct pollution metric.

weak_pairs_not_counted.evidence: Abstract: 'We instantiate the contract on EEGMMI native left/right command-control over 5,400 events ... Provenance blocks C2 routes (0.000); agreement-plus-provenance routes C3 flips (1.000); confirmation-plus-provenance routes them (0.000).' C2 = 'context-only injections, analogous to indirect prompt injection'
weak_pairs_not_counted.note: Self-pair: brain-prompt injection is the paper's own attack family; its C2 (context-only, IPI-analogous) and C3 variants are run with route rates reported. Generic IPI benchmarks themselves are not run.

weak_pairs_not_counted.evidence: Fig. 4: 'Performance comparison on Ledger-QA across varying session counts ... (simulating increasing time horizons)'; ablation: 'MemAgent eventually succumbs to context rot and error accumulation, dropping to ~20%.'
weak_pairs_not_counted.note: Weak/generic pair: measures accuracy as the horizon grows (length-resolved) on its own Ledger-QA and names context rot as what it mitigates; it does not reproduce the registry variants' channels (MCP tool metadata, agentic search tool output).

weak_pairs_not_counted.evidence: Sec. 3.3: 'the Claude Code baseline coordinates agents through a central shared planning context, whereas icat-agent uses synchronous, event-based communication ... icat-agent resolves 67.4% compared with 61.1% by Claude Code'
weak_pairs_not_counted.note: Weak self-pair: the failure is the paper's own coinage (test/patch overfitting from a shared trace); measured only indirectly via SWE-bench Verified/Pro resolve rate against shared-context baselines; overfitting is never counted directly.

weak_pairs_not_counted.evidence: 4.3 Security Assessment: "In the Indirect Prompt Injection test, the baseline model suffered a 96% success rate in SSH key theft, whereas OpenClaw-SRT intercepted 49 out of 50 attempts through its Privacy Gateway's PII masking mechanism"
weak_pairs_not_counted.note: Short workshop paper; IPI test is 50 attempts with sparse description (Cisco Talos attack dataset), but it is a quantitative run against IPI. Missed pair, weak evidence.

weak_pairs_not_counted.evidence: 5.2.1 Case Study 1: 'We tested AgentSight's ability to detect indirect prompt injection attacks[30]. ... The observer LLM analyzed this trace, returned a high-confidence attack score'
weak_pairs_not_counted.note: Weak pair: a single hand-built IPI instance (README -> hidden prompt -> /etc/passwd exfil), detected once; only quantitative numbers are runtime overhead (Table 1).

weak_pairs_not_counted.mechanism: context unawareness (failure to identify a small decisive piece of evidence within long/complex context)
weak_pairs_not_counted.evidence: Mechanism check (Sec. 4/5): 'we evaluate every method on the held-out test set introduced in Fig. 2, and plot selection accuracy'; 3.2: 'On NIAH, standard outcome-based GRPO regresses relative to the base model, whereas CONTEXTRL surpasses the base'
weak_pairs_not_counted.note: The paper coins 'context unawareness' and measures the fix on its own contrastive context probe plus NIAH/LongBench v2; same-paper failure and fix.

weak_pairs_not_counted.evidence: Sec. VII (Table 9): 'TRACER-AI detects all held-out indirect and chained attacks'; Limitations: 'The reported TRACER-AI numerical results are from a controlled synthetic proof-of-concept dataset, not from AgentDojo, InjecAgent, AgentDyn'
weak_pairs_not_counted.note: Weak pair: 500 synthetic template IPI cases scored by a TF-IDF/rule pipeline with no LLM agent executed; it is a quantitative IPI test, but self-built and agent-free.

weak_pairs_not_counted.evidence: 7.2: 'The dataset containing 200 interactions was produced with the help of a custom script ... controlled injection of multi-vector attacks (direct, indirect, multiturn, etc.)'; 7.4.1: 'it performed particularly badly at detecting indirect prompt injections and multi-turn attacks.'
weak_pairs_not_counted.note: Weak pair: tiny self-generated 200-sample set (82 attacks) scored by a TF-IDF classifier and rule engines; IPI is one category, with no per-category number given, only that detection was poor.

no_evaluation_defenses.evidence: Limitations: 'No end-to-end evaluation. The synthetic experiments validate theoretical bounds on abstract paging traces. They do not demonstrate that Neural Paging improves task accuracy when integrated with a real LLM.'
no_evaluation_defenses.note: Theory paper; the only experiments run classical paging heuristics (Belady/LRU/LFU/FIFO/Random) on synthetic Zipf traces; the proposed Page Controller is never trained or measured; lost-in-the-middle is motivation only.

no_evaluation_defenses.defense: PRIMA (context-boundary discipline + reference-material sandboxing + poisoned-output rejection)
no_evaluation_defenses.evidence: Conclusion: 'Quantitative evaluation of the meta-optimization loop, ... domains are left to future work.'; Contributions: 'we describe the design and report architectural properties but leave quantitative effectiveness evaluation to future work.'
no_evaluation_defenses.note: Known reference case: operational-patterns paper with a qualitative Graph Isomorphism case study; IPI countermeasures (context-boundary discipline, sandboxing, poisoned-output rejection) are described, never measured.

no_evaluation_defenses.evidence: Sec. 6.1 Case Study I: 'We successfully detected two attack scenarios.'; Sec. 6.3: 'These comprehensive case studies validate our framework's effectiveness across diverse multi-agent architectures'
no_evaluation_defenses.note: PRIMA-style: two qualitative case studies (CrewAI email assistant with IPI-like email content, Magentic-One) with hand-traced detections; no detection rates, ASR, baselines or trace counts are reported.

no_evaluation_defenses.defense: Ebbinghaus Forgetting Curve Memory Enhancement Framework
no_evaluation_defenses.evidence: 1 Introduction: "the main purpose of this article is to propose a new memory management framework and explain its design principles and verification schemes in detail. Complete system implementation and large-scale empirical evaluation ... will be carried out in the next stage of this study"
no_evaluation_defenses.note: Design + planned LongBench-E protocol (incl. a position-sensitive 'lost in the middle' metric) with only expected gains ('expected to increase by 15-25%'); no results.

no_evaluation_defenses.evidence: Abstract: "we introduce the Full-Lifecycle Agent Security Architecture (FASA). This theoretical defense blueprint advocates for zero-trust agentic execution ... we present Project ClawGuard, our ongoing engineering initiative"
no_evaluation_defenses.note: Threat analysis + risk taxonomy + theoretical architecture; ClawGuard prototype is 'ongoing'; no experiments or numbers.

no_evaluation_defenses.evidence: Abstract: "we present Memory Sandbox, an interactive system and design probe that allows users to manage the conversational memory of LLM-powered agents"; sections are system features (2.1-2.5) and 3 Discussion, no study or measurements
no_evaluation_defenses.note: 2-page HCI demo/design probe: UI affordances to view, hide, edit, summarize and share memory objects; lost in the middle only cited.

no_evaluation_defenses.evidence: 2.1 Research Design: "The benchmark uses calibrated simulation: task success probabilities and decay constants are derived from the theoretical decay model (Definition 2) and author system observation, applied to synthetic sessions"; 2.2: failure modes "are presented as a theoretically grounded conceptual framework rather than as conclusions of a formal empirical study"
no_evaluation_defenses.note: Reports numbers (42% entropy reduction, TCR tables), but they come from a simulation whose success rates and decay constants are set by the authors' own model, not from running agents. Likely the registry's own 'context rot' source paper. Hard call: evaluated_other if simulated numbers count.

no_evaluation_defenses.defense: UNNAMED: Authorization framework for autonomous LLM agent threat mitigation
no_evaluation_defenses.evidence: Abstract: "we propose a theoretical authorization framework, the Context-Aware Agentic Verifiable Policy (CA2P) ... This analysis relies on established cryptographic principles and existing security literature to map the trajectory of agent security"
no_evaluation_defenses.note: Threat model + theoretical authorization design (crypto identity assertions, intent verification); sections are background, threat modeling, framework, discussion, future work; no experiments.

no_evaluation_defenses.defense: MAT-based Assurance Framework (Message-Action Traces + governance layer: capability limits + action mediation)
no_evaluation_defenses.evidence: Sec. I: 'The paper focuses on the methodology, definitions, and metrics required to instantiate an executable evaluation protocol; a full empirical study is ongoing but is not reported here.'
no_evaluation_defenses.note: Methodology/framework paper: defines Message-Action Traces, contracts, stress-testing and fault-injection protocol (incl. IPI as bounded perturbation) and metrics; no results.

no_evaluation_defenses.evidence: Conclusion/limitations: 'We also note that this paper does not include experiments. Whether SDO prevents the failures we describe in practice is a question that can only be answered by building and evaluating it'
no_evaluation_defenses.note: Position paper: proposes SDO design and walks through a hypothetical e-commerce case study (Sec. 3.3); nothing is implemented or measured.

unsure.evidence: III.A Indirect Injection Attack Surface: "the context xc is an aggregation of the authoritative system rules Psys, a logical separator z, and the untrusted user input Puser ... An indirect PIA constitutes the adversarial construction of a contaminated input sequence P*user"; Sec. IV reports Base ASR 70.0% vs Defense ASR <1%
unsure.note: Quantitative ASR evaluation (10 .cursorrules x 9 payloads) which the authors call indirect PIA, but payloads are placed in the user-input slot, not in retrieved/external content; Limitations admit payloads in README/JSON files are not covered. Ran-named only if user-slot payloads count as IPI.
